jobs.title: Executive Communications Director, Chief Product & Technology Officer
jobs.text:
Who we are
At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.
Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
.
Hiring and how we work
We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!
Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.
.
See yourself at Twilio
Join the team as Twilio’s next Executive Communications Director, Chief Product & Technology Officer.
About the job
Twilio is an innovation-driven company on a transformative journey, and we are seeking an executive communications director to be the trusted communications partner for Twilio’s Chief Product & Technology Officer In this highly visible and strategic role, you will craft and drive impactful messaging that elevates the CPTO’s voice across internal and external audiences, reinforcing Twilio’s vision, product strategy, and leadership in the industry. You will also selectively support the R&D organization and leadership team on various initiatives to share Twilio’s innovation story, both internally and externally.
This role sits within Twilio’s corporate communications team, responsible for shaping and delivering Twilio’s story across investors, press, customers, industry analysts, and employees. You will develop executive-level content and thought leadership, manage internal and external communications, and support change management initiatives to ensure clarity, alignment, and engagement across Twilio’s R&D organization and beyond.
Responsibilities
In this role, you’ll:
Iterate and execute an annual executive communications strategy and plan that positions the Chief Product & Technology Officer as the transformative leader behind Twilio’s innovation story.
Take the pen on all content coming from Twilio’s CPTO including keynotes, internal presentations, blogs, press and social media.
Partner with PMM and CorpComms on impactful, forward-thinking communications that tell Twilio’s innovation story from various R&D leaders
Propose opportunities and concepts for thought leadership to elevate Twilio’s R&D leadership’s visibility in the market
Develop content to represent R&D at quarterly Company All Hands meetings and other key internal companywide meetings
Drive communications for ongoing change management initiatives within the R&D function
Develop content for R&D function-level communications and events that supports Twilio’s unique Builder culture.
Build and maintain relationships with key partners to inform CPTO communications strategy including Twilio’s Management Team, R&D Leadership, Corporate Communications, Product Marketing, and more.
Qualifications
Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!
*Required:
10+ years experience in communications, including a minimum 3 years in a dedicated executive communications role
5+ years in the tech industry
Desired:
Experience writing for, working directly with and influencing CEOs, C-level executives, and SVPs
Strong executive presence and ability to advise on communications strategy to all levels of the organization
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills with the ability to partner effectively across R&D, GTM, Marketing, HR, PR, and Internal Comms teams
Excellent project management skills
Strong business acumen with exemplary editing and writing skills
Experience in external-facing thought leadership (blogs, event keynotes, social media)
Proficiency in creating slide desks for large audience presentations
Strong ability to synthesize complex topics (AI, data, product strategy) into compelling, digestible content for diverse audiences
Exceptional writing and storytelling skills with the ability to craft clear, engaging, and strategic messaging for executive leaders.
Location
This role will be remote and based in the West Coast, USA.
Travel
We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 25% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.
What We Offer
Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.
Compensation
*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.
The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:
Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont or Washington D.C. : $171,120 - $213,900.
Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $181,200 - $226,500.
Based in the San Francisco Bay area, California: $201,280 - $251,600.
This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.
The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.
Application deadline information (required for ALL US jobs)
Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until October 31, 2026, but may change based on business needs.
Twilio thinks big. Do you?
We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.
So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.
.
Stay alert to recruitment fraud
We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.
.
Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.text:
Salary: Up to £85,000 per annum + Annual Bonus
Hours: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Location: Warrington/London with regular travel across the Healthcare LIFT portfolio
Benefits: 25 days AL + BH, Life Insurance, Car Allowance, Pension Scheme, Employee Assistance Programme, salary sacrifice schemes, gym & retailer discounts.
Kudos Services is a specialist facilities management provider delivering high-quality Hard FM services across complex healthcare environments. We are looking for an experienced and dynamic Head of Engineering to lead our Engineering & Maintenance team across our Healthcare LIFT portfolio.
Key Requirements
Significant experience managing Hard FM services across complex, multi-site estates within a PPP/PFI environment, ideally healthcare.
Strong technical knowledge of building services engineering, statutory compliance and healthcare maintenance requirements, including HTMs and HBNs.
Proven leadership experience managing engineering teams, contractors and multiple stakeholders.
Commercially aware, with experience of performance management, contract delivery and budget accountability.
HNC/HND (or equivalent) in a Mechanical, Electrical or Building Services Engineering discipline.
About the Role
Reporting directly to the CEO, this is a senior leadership role responsible for the strategic and operational management of Engineering & Maintenance services across our Healthcare LIFT portfolio.
You will lead the Engineering Team, ensuring the safe, compliant and effective delivery of Hard FM services whilst maintaining high levels of customer satisfaction and contractual performance. Working closely with Contract Managers and the Compliance Team, you will oversee statutory compliance, technical governance, engineering performance and quality assurance across the estate.
You will act as the lead representative for engineering audits and technical reviews, ensuring robust processes, clear audit trails and full compliance with contractual and statutory obligations. The role will also take ownership of engineering reporting, resource planning, contractor performance, asset management and lifecycle activities.
As a key member of the senior leadership team, you will contribute to commercial and financial performance, supporting budget setting, forecasting, procurement activities and business-wide continuous improvement initiatives.
About You
You are an experienced engineering leader who combines strong technical expertise with excellent people management and stakeholder engagement skills. You thrive in complex, highly regulated environments and have a proven track record of delivering engineering services within healthcare, PPP or PFI contracts.
You are commercially aware, solutions-focused and capable of balancing strategic priorities with day-to-day operational demands. You are committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality and compliance whilst developing strong working relationships with colleagues, clients and partners.
Most importantly, you are a proactive leader who can inspire teams, drive performance and support the continued success of our healthcare portfolio.
Our Values:
Supportive - We embrace partnership working.
Ethical - We act with integrity.
Innovative - We take ownership for understanding and improving our business.
Ambitious - We continually strive to deliver the best possible service.
Passionate - We are proud of the part we play and the service we deliver.
Application Process:
Application & CV Screening
First Stage Interview Head of HR & Kudos CEO
Final Stage Interview Asset CEO/Director & FIM CEO
As part of the recruitment process, you may be required to complete a profiling assessment and/or a role-specific scenario based assessment.

jobs.title: Director, Security Engineering
jobs.text:
Fireblocks is the company bringing global finance onchain. Backed by over $1 billion in capital, we are the premier digital asset infrastructure provider trusted by thousands of industry-defining financial institutions, including banks, payment providers, fintechs, and global corporates such as BNY Mellon, BNP Paribas, ANZ Bank, Western Union, Stripe, and Revolut. Built for institutional scale and security, our enterprise-grade platform and network have powered over $14 trillion in digital asset transfers worldwide.
The world of digital assets is accelerating in speed, magnitude, and complexity, opening the door to new ways for leveraging the blockchain. Fireblocks’ platform and network provide the simplest and most secure way for companies to work with digital assets and is trusted by some of the largest financial institutions, banks, globally-recognized brands, and Web3 companies in the world, including BNY Mellon, BNP Paribas, ANZ Bank, Revolut, and thousands more.
About the Role
As Director of Security Engineering, you will lead the modernization of Fireblocks’ security infrastructure — across both our in-house-built tooling and the SaaS platforms we rely on. You will own the architecture behind security operations, our security data lake, SaaS security, and cloud security, and build the infrastructure that makes Fireblocks’ security tooling faster, more efficient, and ready for an agentic operating model.
This is a hands-on leadership role: you will set the technical direction, build out a team and processes, and personally drive projects from architecture through implementation and measurable impact.
What You’ll Do
Security Infrastructure Strategy & Modernization
Own the multi-year modernization roadmap for Fireblocks’ security infrastructure, spanning in-house tooling and SaaS.
Analyze the needs across security domains, ensure we have the appropriate architecture for a centralized security data lake, and propose and drive optimized designs for agentic flows.
Security Data & Detection Engineering
Build and evolve Fireblocks’ security data lake and the logging, detection, and analytics pipelines built on top of it.
Optimize security data infrastructure to support faster detection, detailed investigation and automated response.
Cross-Functional Leadership
Coordinate and align with Security, R&D, and DevOps stakeholders to drive infrastructure projects end-to-end.
Lead projects from concept to delivery, and define the metrics that demonstrate their impact.
Requirements
7+ years of progressive cybersecurity experience, including leadership roles in SecOps, Application Security, or DevSecOps.
At least 3–4 years in a formal leadership or management capacity.
Security Engineering background — hands-on experience implementing and optimizing security systems is a must.
Proven experience building security systems and workflows that handle large-scale data (e.g., security data lakes, SIEM), including hands-on work with security auditing, logging, and cloud infrastructure.
Hands-on experience implementing AI processes, workflows, and tools to optimize security operations and workflows, and familiarity with AI security tooling.
Strong track record coordinating across Security, R&D, and DevOps stakeholders.
A builder mentality: the desire and ability to create infrastructure from scratch, lead projects end-to-end, and measure their impact.
Nice to Have
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field.
Professional certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCSP).

jobs.title: Director of Hardware Engineering & Manufacturing
jobs.text:
About Us
InnerPlant is on a mission to transform farming as never before imagined: We give crops a voice by turning plants into living sensors that signal the onset of stress, enabling farmers to increase yields and reduce costs by optimizing inputs.
The Director of Hardware Engineering & Manufacturing is responsible for the hardware systems that power InnerPlant's commercial product, CropVoice. The CropVoice platform translates signals from our living sensors to pinpoint stress well before visible symptoms, giving farmers and agronomists critical and timely insights and removing the guesswork behind key in-season decisions. The Director owns the hardware product lifecycle—from architecture and engineering through prototyping, validation, manufacturing, deployment, and continuous improvement—as InnerPlant turns breakthrough technology into scalable, reliable products that can operate across millions of acres.
The Director of Hardware Engineering & Manufacturing will be based in Des Moines, IA, and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.
Your Role
As the Director of Hardware Engineering & Manufacturing, you will lead the development, production, and integration of the hardware behind CropVoice—working at the cutting edge of precision agriculture, electronics, optical sensing, mechanical design, and manufacturing. You will shape how InnerPlant's hardware function grows. As the CropVoice platform scales across crops and geographies, you will have the mandate to build and lead the hardware engineering organization. To achieve success, you will:
Lead hardware product design and development, including:
Owning the hardware engineering roadmap and system architecture for CropVoice's optical, electrical, embedded, mechanical, and data-acquisition systems;
Leading development from concept and rapid prototyping through design verification, validation, production, and field deployment;
Overseeing design of hardware that meets product and field requirements and operates reliably through heat, cold, moisture, dust, vibration, variable power conditions, long operating hours, and limited opportunities for maintenance;
Overseeing equipment operation to ensure the efficiency and reliability of CropVoice hardware and troubleshoot when needed; and
Using field data and customer feedback to continuously improve product performance.
Drive efficient and scalable manufacturing processes, including:
Owning the transition of hardware products from engineering prototypes into repeatable and scalable manufacturing, anchored in design-for-manufacturing and design-for-assembly practices;
Developing and managing relationships with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and strategic technology partners, and building scalable and cost-effective supply-chain strategies for critical components and assemblies;
Establishing manufacturing processes, quality standards, test procedures, and production controls, and leading root-cause analysis and corrective action for manufacturing and field failures; and
Establishing reliability and environmental testing programs and verification and validation strategies.
Build the hardware engineering team:
Establish engineering processes that enable rapid development without compromising product quality or reliability; and
Recruit, develop, mentor, and lead a high-performing hardware engineering team with clear technical ownership, accountability, priorities, and development processes.
What Makes You Stand Out
The successful Director of Hardware Engineering & Manufacturing is both a technical leader and a builder: someone who can establish engineering discipline while moving quickly, solve difficult problems personally when necessary, and work across the organization to turn ambitious technology into products that work reliably in the real world. In particular, you will have demonstrated the ability to:
Solve technically challenging projects with strategic management of people, programs, and resources and be willing to dive deeply into technical problems when needed.
Translate between highly technical disciplines and business objectives, working closely with software and data engineering, plant science and biotechnology, agronomy, product, commercial, and field operations teams so that hardware development remains tightly connected to customer value and commercial priorities.
Champion the company's mission to transform farming and create an engineering culture that values speed, technical excellence, experimentation, ownership, and learning.
Drive continuous improvement in product quality, cost, and reliability as InnerPlant's commercial footprint grows.

jobs.title: CTO (Chief Technology Officer)
jobs.text:
📋 DESCRIPTION (About Norbloc + Why This Role Matters + What You'll Own)
Norbloc builds the trust infrastructure behind modern financial compliance. Our RegTech and blockchain platform powers Know Your Customer (KYC) and secure data-sharing for banks, financial institutions and government bodies, replacing slow, fragmented, manual onboarding with a shared, distributed-ledger-backed ecosystem that regulators, banks and customers can all rely on.
Our clients are not forgiving of shortcuts: systemic banks, regulators and government bodies across Europe and the Middle East operate under some of the strictest security, resilience and compliance standards in the industry. Building for them means every architectural choice has to hold up under real scrutiny.
We're now looking for a Chief Technology Officer to take that foundation and scale it, leading technology through Norbloc's next phase of growth.
Why This Role Matters Now
Norbloc sits where two worlds meet: the pace and ambition of blockchain and data innovation versus the risk tolerance of enterprise banking. Few technology leaders are fluent in both. This role exists to be that bridge, someone who can architect for scale and security, lead engineering teams through rapid growth and sit across the table from a bank's CIO or a regulator's compliance officer and speak their language fluently.
This is a board-level seat with real ownership: over architecture, over the technology organization and over how Norbloc is perceived by the institutions that matter most to our growth.
What You'll Own
Technology Strategy & Architecture
Set Norbloc's end-to-end technology strategy and multi-quarter roadmap, in step with company vision and enterprise client needs
Architect secure, cloud-native systems that bridge banking-grade infrastructure with blockchain/DLT, cryptography and modern data and AI capabilities
Own the platform's operating model, including SLAs, observability, incident response and on-call practices, to a standard that satisfies regulated financial clients, not just internal targets
Make build-vs-buy and vendor/platform calls backed by clear-eyed cost, scalability and governance analysis. Be willing to defend the "boring" choice when it's the right one
Data, Governance & Compliance
Build the data governance, lineage, metadata and quality foundations that make the platform auditable and trustworthy at scale
Own technology risk management and IT governance, including compliance with KYC/AML, data residency and audit requirements across our operating jurisdictions
Work with Compliance and external legal counsel so that technical decisions are made with regulatory consequences already priced in, not discovered afterward
Team & Delivery Leadership
Lead, mentor and scale Engineering, Data, DevOps and QA, building strong managers under you, not just individual contributors
Instill the delivery discipline that enterprise clients expect: code quality, CI/CD, testing rigor, predictable roadmaps
Take ownership of any externally delivered components and bring them fully in-house where it makes sense to do so
Executive & Client Engagement
Be Norbloc's senior technical voice to C-level executives, IT leadership and compliance officers at bank and government clients
Represent Norbloc's technology vision to investors, partners and prospective enterprise clients
Translate technical trade-offs (cost, risk, scalability) into terms a systemic bank's leadership can act on with confidence

jobs.title: VP of Engineering
jobs.text:
Location: Bangalore, India (Hybrid) — regular travel expected, primarily to China, with occasional travel to the UK
Department: Technology
WHO WE ARE
At Acclaro, we're more than a localization company — we're a content intelligence solutions company, and a global team of language enthusiasts, cultural connectors, and technology innovators. Our mission is to help brands speak the world's languages and resonate deeply across cultures by blending human expertise with cutting-edge technology, delivered through a follow-the-sun model that keeps our teams moving around the clock and around the globe.
With over two decades of experience, we support some of the world's most recognizable brands in expanding their global reach. And we're scaling: we've been making material investments in our own AI-native platform, one that's already reshaping how our business — and the localization industry more broadly — works. Join us on our journey to be the model localization company of the next decade, one that's loved by clients, colleagues, and communities alike.
YOUR NEXT ROLE
As VP of Engineering, you'll lead the strategy, execution, and evolution of Acclaro's technology organization with the visibility and mandate to shape engineering as a core driver of the business. You'll lead a globally distributed engineering team across China and India.
You're joining at a pivotal moment, Acclaro is undergoing a major structural transformation, building our own proprietary AI platform to stay competitive, and evolving into a truly tech-enabled company. This role sits at the center of that shift — you'll help build new technology from the ground up while keeping our existing systems running reliably through the transition.
This is not a delegation-only leadership position. You'll stay connected to architecture, technical decision-making, and day-to-day engineering reality while building high-performing global teams. If you thrive at the intersection of technology, leadership, and business impact, and want the kind of ownership that comes from building something rather than inheriting it, this is that opportunity.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
Lead the engineering organization, providing strategic direction while staying hands-on in architecture, system design, and technical decision-making — including participating directly in code reviews and technical debugging when it matters
Lead the build-out of Acclaro's new proprietary AI platform alongside the modernization of existing systems, balancing green-field development with operational continuity through a major technology transformation
Partner with Product, Design, and business leaders to translate company priorities into scalable execution plans and technology roadmaps
Drive architectural reviews and major technology decisions, balancing innovation, scalability, reliability, security, and maintainability
Establish and continuously improve engineering standards, development practices, CI/CD processes, and quality frameworks
Own engineering performance, reliability, uptime, delivery predictability, and platform health through measurable goals and KPIs
Build, develop, and mentor engineering leaders, creating clear career paths, growth opportunities, and succession plans across the organization
Lead workforce planning, organizational design, and hiring for critical engineering leadership and senior technical positions
Be personally present during major incidents — not just briefed afterward — and own disaster recovery planning, security readiness, and business continuity
Manage engineering budgets, infrastructure investments, vendor relationships, and build-versus-buy decisions
Ensure technology practices align with security, privacy, and data protection requirements across global markets
Represent engineering at the executive level, providing visibility into progress, risks, capacity, and investment priorities
Serve as a trusted technical voice with clients, partners, and external stakeholders when required
THIS ROLE IS FOR YOU IF YOU
Have 10+ years in engineering leadership, including 5+ years at the senior executive level
Hold a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent professional experience
Bring a strong, current technical foundation that lets you engage confidently in architecture discussions, technical reviews, and critical production incidents — not just receive summaries of them
Have a proven track record building and scaling enterprise-grade platforms or integrated technology ecosystems
Are experienced with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP), APIs, microservices, and modern development practices like CI/CD
Bring expertise integrating enterprise systems such as TMS, CMS, CRM, or workflow automation tools
Have led distributed engineering teams across multiple countries, cultures, and time zones, and thrive leading remote, globally distributed teams
Thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments where strategy and execution go hand-in-hand
Are an exceptional communicator who can adapt complex technical concepts for executive, customer, and non-technical audiences, and who leads with clarity and empathy
YOU’LL STAND OUT IF YOU
Have hands-on experience with localization technologies or global content platforms
Bring knowledge of AI/ML-driven automation and its application to localization or content workflows
Have led modernization projects that transformed legacy systems into scalable, integrated solutions
Are multilingual or have deep experience working across distributed, multicultural teams
Understand global compliance and security frameworks such as GDPR, SOC 2, or ISO certifications
Have launched and scaled a new platform within a transformative business environment
INCLUSION & EQUAL OPPORTUNITY - Acclaro is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.text:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
As a Field CTO, Public Sector at GitLab, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor for public sector customers and prospects, helping them connect DevSecOps strategy, security, and compliance goals to real business and mission outcomes. You will work closely with executive stakeholders during the pre-sales process, offering strategic guidance on how GitLab can support secure software delivery, modernization efforts, and platform adoption across complex environments.
In this role, you will combine technical depth with executive communication. You will build relationships with leaders such as Chief Information Security Officers, Chief Security Officers, Chief Technology Officers, and chief security architects, while also partnering across GitLab with sales, marketing, and product teams. Your perspective from the field will help shape customer conversations, influence go-to-market strategy, and inform how GitLab continues to serve public sector organizations.
Note: This is an individual contributor, customer-facing technical advisory role; it does not include direct people management responsibilities.
This role is well suited for someone who enjoys operating at the intersection of technology strategy, customer engagement, and market leadership. You will help customers understand the value of a single DevSecOps platform, contribute to industry conversations around standards and guidance, and represent GitLab in a way that reflects our values of transparency, collaboration, and results.
Some examples of our projects:
Supporting strategic public sector opportunities with executive-level DevSecOps and security guidance
Contributing to government working groups, standards discussions, and public sector thought leadership content
What you'll do
Engage with customers in a technical consulting and advisory role during the pre-sales process, providing technical assistance and strategic guidance.
Deliver executive-level thought leadership on DevSecOps, security, and compliance for strategic public sector opportunities, including new and growth accounts.
Build and maintain relationships with customer leaders such as Chief Information Security Officers, Chief Security Officers, Chief Technology Officers, and chief security architects.
Partner with the marketing team to develop content and support media engagement opportunities that increase awareness of GitLab in the public sector market.
Educate customers on the value of the GitLab platform and related technologies, and support conversations across multiple levels of the organization to help enable successful deployment.
Assist with requests for information and responses related to government publications and public-private partnership opportunities.
Participate in and contribute to working groups connected to government publications, standards, and demonstrations.
Curate and communicate public sector field feedback, collaborate on prioritization with marketing and product teams, and contribute to sales strategy, playbooks, enablement, and reusable technical content for the field.
What you'll bring
Demonstrated expertise in DevSecOps strategy, application security, and compliance for regulated environments, including providing risk-based guidance.
Experience selling to, supporting, or working within the public sector.
Experience creating and delivering technical thought leadership content (presentations, demos, written materials) independently.
Working knowledge of the end-to-end software development lifecycle, including CI/CD and modern engineering and operations practices.
Experience with cloud computing and modern platform architectures that support secure software delivery.
Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate technical strategy effectively to audiences ranging from executives to engineers.
Comfort working in a fully remote, distributed, and asynchronous environment.
Ability to coordinate across time zones and adapt schedules to customer and internal stakeholder needs.
Experience in technical pre-sales, consulting, solutions architecture, or comparable customer-facing IT roles, including using GitLab (and willingness to learn quickly) to support customer conversations and demonstrations.
Living in the Washington D.C. Metro area preferred
Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, as permitted by applicable law.
About the team
The Field CTO, Public Sector role works across customer-facing and internal teams to help GitLab meet the needs of public sector organizations with clarity, credibility, and deep technical insight. This role partners closely with sales, solutions, marketing, and product stakeholders to represent customer priorities, strengthen technical strategy in the field, and support GitLab's position in a highly regulated and mission-driven market.
The team environment is collaborative, remote, and asynchronous, with a strong focus on sharing knowledge and turning field insight into action. The work is especially meaningful because it brings together executive advisory skills, platform expertise, and an understanding of security and compliance expectations that matter in public sector environments. Success in this role comes from being able to translate complex technical topics into clear guidance, while also helping GitLab improve how we serve this market over time.
At GitLab, you'll do this work in a values-driven culture built on collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency.

jobs.text:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
As Director, Product Management: Agentic Software Delivery, you'll own one of GitLab's most strategic sections, spanning Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability. You'll lead senior and principal product managers and be accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue across build, package, deploy, and monitor. Today, these are separate stages with a human making the call at each handoff. As agents take on more coding, pipeline, and deployment work, you'll set the three-year vision for how much of that judgment the system can make safely and how quickly a production signal can turn into a fix without waiting for a human to notice it first. You'll define how customers move from today's manual checkpoints toward agent-driven software delivery at a pace that fits their risk tolerance. In your first year, you'll bring four connected roadmaps into one coherent strategy, establish how investment is allocated and reallocated, deepen partnerships with Engineering and go-to-market leaders, and give customers a credible path for managing software delivery at scale.
What you’ll do
Own the strategy, three-year vision, and business outcomes for GitLab's Agentic Software Delivery section, with a clear point of view on how artificial intelligence is changing software delivery.
Lead and develop senior and principal product managers across Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability, helping them grow as independent decision-makers.
Establish the frameworks, standards, and operating rhythm that support consistent, high-quality product decisions without unnecessary escalation.
Own section-level key performance indicators and adoption funnels, using the results to reallocate investment or stop work that isn't paying off.
Evaluate major strategic bets, partnerships, and build, buy, or partner decisions, and develop the business cases that support them.
Partner with Engineering leadership on platform investment, architectural direction, and trade-offs across the section, while connecting build, package, deploy, and monitor into one coherent customer experience.
Drive pricing, packaging, go-to-market strategy, migration, and adoption with Product Marketing, Sales, Pricing, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.
Represent the section with GitLab's senior leadership, key enterprise customers, partners, and industry audiences, while modeling AI-native product management across discovery, synthesis, prototyping, roadmap exploration, and concept development.
What you’ll bring
Experience leading product managers, including developing senior and principal talent, hiring, and addressing performance directly.
A track record of owning a portfolio across multiple product areas and being accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue, not only roadmap delivery.
Product management depth in one or more relevant areas, such as continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, artifact or package management, release management, or observability.
Sound judgment about where to invest and where to stop, including experience making and defending build, buy, or partner decisions with a business case.
Technical fluency to work with engineers and architects on pipeline design, artifact workflows, deployment strategies, and observability signals such as logs, metrics, and traces.
Experience shaping pricing and packaging for technical products across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.
Experience working with technical customers in developer tools, DevOps, or software delivery environments where engineers and engineering leaders are primary users.
Executive-level communication and influence.
Practical use of AI tools in product management workflows, along with a thoughtful view of how AI and agentic workflows are changing software delivery. We welcome candidates whose experience may come from different but transferable product and leadership paths.
About the team
The team brings together senior product leaders across GitLab's software delivery platform and works closely with Engineering, Design, and go-to-market partners so customers experience these capabilities as one connected system. The team helps customers manage today's delivery complexity while shaping how AI-powered and AI-native workflows influence the next generation of software delivery. As part of GitLab's all-remote organization, the team collaborates asynchronously across regions with a focus on transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.
The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.text:
We are seeking a highly technical, hands-on, and battle-tested Head of Engineering to lead our core engineering teams as we scale our real-time verification and decision engines across Southeast Asia. In this role, you will bridge high-level system architecture with deep operational rigor.
You are not an abstract manager—you are an active technical leader who regularly participates in system design reviews, inspects critical PRs, fine-tunes performance bottlenecks, and drives incident management alongside your team. You will set the high mark for execution speed, engineering craftsmanship, system resilience, and clear communication across cross-functional product and business units.
Key Responsibilities
Lead system design, high-availability architecture, and API scalability across microservices, eKYC/eKYB pipelines, and database infrastructure.
Debug high-severity production incidents, conduct root-cause analysis, and improve database efficiency, lock contention, and system latency.
Lead live system migrations and zero-downtime maintenance strategies, including dual-write backfills and atomic cutovers.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Engineering
jobs.text:
The big picture: Axios is a modern media company built around clarity, trust, and smart, essential coverage. As AI reshapes how companies operate, Axios has an opportunity to become more AI-native in how we build products, improve workflows, and help teams move faster with better judgment. We are hiring a Sr. Director of Engineering to lead the people, systems, and practices behind reliable products.
Why it matters: This leader will develop engineering managers and senior technical leaders while closely guiding teams using AI to build and experiment. Working closely with the CTO, you will turn company technology direction into clear engineering decisions and execution.
Go deeper: The role spans engineering across Axios products, platforms, and workflows, from our CMS and axios.com to newsletters, Local products, internal tools, and systems supporting the Newsroom and business teams. Product, Newsroom, and business leaders set the goals. Engineering builds the systems and capabilities that help achieve them. The right leader will speed decisions, shorten the path from idea to product, spot risks early, and escalate issues before they grow. Responsibilities include:
Partner closely with the CTO and engineering leaders to shape engineering strategy and technical direction.
Lead and develop engineering managers and senior technical leaders, supporting clear accountability and a healthy culture. Develop and retain strong talent, and hire thoughtfully as needs evolve.
Strengthen planning, delivery, quality, and reliability. Help teams make faster decisions, move ideas into products, spot risks, and escalate issues early.
Partner with Product, Design, Newsroom, and business leaders to turn priorities into technical plans and match engineering capacity to the most important work.
Bring strong judgment to architecture, platforms, and reliability, especially when tradeoffs span teams.
Own the operating standards, guidelines, and practices that help engineering teams plan, build, test, release, operate, and learn effectively.
Establish shared benchmarks and baselines for engineering health.
Lead vendor evaluation and selection for engineering tools, platforms, and services, balancing capability, cost, security, reliability, support, and long-term fit.
Help define modern engineering leadership inside an AI-native media company and shape how Axios builds, learns, and delivers at speed.
Worthy of your time: This leader must be a close partner to the CTO and senior leaders who can explain technical details clearly and dive deep with engineers on technical and architectural questions. Success means faster decisions, a shorter path from idea to product, strong engineering leadership, reliable systems, and an organization that sees around corners. What we’re looking for:
You have led and developed engineering managers and senior technical leaders, setting clear expectations and addressing performance directly.
You have helped teams use AI to improve how they build, test, and operate software and to experiment with new product capabilities.
You translate technical details for executives and nontechnical partners while going deep with engineers on technical and architectural questions.
You quickly understand unfamiliar areas, ask the right questions, and know when to bring in expertise, invest in platforms, simplify systems, or accept a short-term tradeoff.
Ideally, you have led teams responsible for high-traffic digital products and the platforms behind them.
You have a strong vision for how AI and technology will change engineering practices, product development, platforms, and internal workflows.
Starting salary for this role is in the range of $250,000 - $270,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation benefits. Axios' compensation philosophy takes into account the cost of labor differentials across the country. Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.
Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.
What Axios brings to the table besides salary:
401(k) with employer match
Robust PPO and high-deductible health insurance options on the Blue Cross Blue Shield network
Employer Health Savings Account (HSA) contribution for the high-deductible health plan option
Dental and vision coverage
Primary caregiver 12-week paid leave
Generous vacation policy, plus holidays
One mental health day per quarter
Annual learning and development stipend
$100 monthly work-from-home stipend
Tele-mental health services through Headspace
OneMedical membership, including telehealth services
Personal health advocacy resources through HealthAdvocate
Inclusive fertility, hormonal health and family-forming benefits through Carrot Fertility
Access to the Axios “Family Fund”, which was created to allow employees to request financial support when facing financial hardship or emergencies
Increased work flexibility for parents and caretakers
Virtual company-sponsored social events
A strong and positive work environment
A commitment to an open, inclusive, and diverse work culture
Equal Opportunity Employer Statement
Axios is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.
This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. Axios makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

jobs.title: Head of App Development
jobs.text:
Releaf Dispensary Ltd is a pioneering medical cannabis clinic committed to providing high-quality, safe, and effective cannabis-based products. Headquartered in the UK, we aim to enhance the quality of life for our patients through cutting-edge solutions and outstanding patient service. We are a fast-growing team of passionate professionals on a mission to put patients back in control of their health journey — we have seen first-hand how alternative treatments can change lives.
About the Role
Releaf is looking for an experienced Head of App Development to lead the strategy, architecture and delivery of our native iOS and Android applications. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has built and scaled consumer-facing health or wellness apps, and who understands how to turn complex clinical and patient data into simple, trustworthy mobile experiences.
You will own our app roadmap end to end from technical architecture through to App Store and Google Play release. A core part of this role is our use of health and wearable data: you will need deep, practical experience working with Apple HealthKit, the Apple Health app, and Apple Watch data, alongside equivalent experience on Android with Health Connect and Wear OS.
This is a rare opportunity to shape the mobile experience for a fast-growing healthcare business, working at the intersection of clinical care, patient engagement and consumer-grade product design.
You'll work with a designer to create the UI/UX and then develop it with the developers to connect it to the backend of our bespoke system.Using API. We have a team of over 20 developers.
What You'll Be Doing
Owning the technical strategy, development and roadmap for Releaf's native iOS and Android applications
Leading the design and implementation of features built on Apple HealthKit and the Apple Health app, including reading, writing and visualising health data
Integrating Apple Watch data — including activity, heart rate, sleep and other relevant metrics — into patient-facing features in a clear, intuitive UI
Building equivalent health data experiences on Android using Health Connect and Wear OS, ensuring feature parity across platforms
Working closely with Product, Design, Clinical and Data Protection teams to ensure features are clinically sound, intuitive, and fully compliant with healthcare data regulations
Owning app performance, stability, release management and the end-to-end App Store / Google Play submission process
Establishing engineering best practice across testing, CI/CD, code review and security for mobile
Staying ahead of platform changes from Apple and Google — particularly around HealthKit, Health Connect, privacy frameworks and wearable APIs — and advising the business on their implications
Contributing to the wider technology strategy as a senior member of the engineering leadership team
What We're Looking For
Essential
Proven experience leading native app development for both iOS and Android, ideally including time as a senior or lead engineer before moving into management
Hands-on experience building features using Apple HealthKit and integrating with the Apple Health app
Direct experience working with Apple Watch/health data (healthkit) — reading and presenting metrics such as heart rate, activity rings, sleep or workout data within a consumer app
Working knowledge of the Android equivalent stack — Health Connect and Wear OS — and experience building comparable cross-platform health features
Portfolio of apps that we can test the UI and functionality.
Strong understanding of mobile UI/UX principles, particularly around presenting health data in a way that is clear, reassuring and easy to act on
Experience managing the full app lifecycle, including App Store and Google Play submission, review processes, and ongoing release management
A track record of building, leading and growing high-performing engineering teams
Comfortable working in a regulated environment, with an understanding of data protection and patient privacy considerations (UK GDPR, or equivalent)
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders
Desirable
Experience in healthcare, digital health, or a regulated consumer product environment
Familiarity with Swift/SwiftUI and Kotlin/Jetpack Compose at a technical depth sufficient to review architecture and code where needed
Experience with remote patient monitoring, chronic condition management apps, or similar health-tracking products
Exposure to clinical safety standards or medical device software regulations (e.g. UKCA/MHRA, IEC 62304) is a strong plus, though not required
Experience working alongside clinical teams to validate the safety and accuracy of health-related features
We’re looking for someone who is excited to join a busy growing organisation - our team culture is based on support and respect and we take a proactive approach to employee progression and development. The ideal candidate for this role will be happy to roll their sleeves up and can take ownership of this role. In return, we offer flexible working; personalised training and development; private health insurance, Employee Assistance Programmes; access to employee perks and Releaf staff patient benefits.
Our application process starts off with an informal remote meeting followed by a written test. We are an inclusive employer and would welcome applications from a diverse range of applicants; if there is anything we can do to help support you during the interview process, please let us know.
At Releaf, we believe that diverse teams build better businesses. We're committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected, and able to do their best work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences — and we're happy to make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process if you need them. If you'd like to discuss this, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering, Rewards
jobs.text:
Who we are
Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.
Why Poland
Poland is a new and deliberate addition to our engineering map. We recently made our first technology hire in the country, and we see it as a long-term strategic location for senior hires, particularly within engineering. Joining now means joining early, and helping shape what our presence here becomes.
So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in Poland.
About The Role
Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people.
Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale.
The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve.
This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader.
Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs.
You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes:
Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end.
Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority.
Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents.
Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales.
Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour.
Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives.
Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned.
Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience.
Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands.
Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them.
Who You Are
Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role.
Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs.
Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them.
At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team.
Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead.
10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases.
Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits.
Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers.
Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work.
Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required.
Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement.
Cultural Alignment
As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.
Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets.
Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality.
Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality.
Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early.
Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders.
No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes.
Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not.
Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.
What Success Looks Like In The Role
The existing cashback product performing measurably better — faster, more reliable, and more compelling to customers.
A credible rewards platform roadmap defined with Product, and the first initiatives beyond cashback shipped.
A functioning experimentation practice, where the team ships, measures and learns on a short cycle.
An engineering organisation built out from its current base, with a strong bench of Engineering Managers and senior engineers.
Rewards established as a measurable contributor to retention and engagement across the customer base.
Clear architecture standards and engineering processes in place across the product units.
Why Join Us
A rare blank page. The platform exists, but almost everything it could become is still ahead of it, and you will define what that is.
Direct influence on retention across a base of roughly 23 million users, at one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa.
Full autonomy as the CTO of your domain, with the backing to build the organisation you think the problem needs.
Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals.
What To Expect In The Hiring Process
60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers.
60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes.
60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business.
60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager).
Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.
#LI-Remote

blocks.text: Who we are

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.
Why Poland

Poland is a new and deliberate addition to our engineering map. We recently made our first technology hire in the country, and we see it as a long-term strategic location for senior hires, particularly within engineering. Joining now means joining early, and helping shape what our presence here becomes.
So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in Poland.
About The Role

Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people.

Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale.

The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve.

This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader.

Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs.

You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes:

items: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end.
Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority.
Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents.
Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales.
Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour.
Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives.
Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned.

Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience.
Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands.
Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them.

blocks.text: Who You Are

items: Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role.
Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs.

Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them.
At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team.
Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead.
10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases.
Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits.
Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers.
Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work.
Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required.
Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement.

blocks.text: Cultural Alignment

As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.

items: Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets.
Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality.
Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality.
Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early.
Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders.
No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes.
Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not.
Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.

blocks.text: What Success Looks Like In The Role

items: The existing cashback product performing measurably better — faster, more reliable, and more compelling to customers.
A credible rewards platform roadmap defined with Product, and the first initiatives beyond cashback shipped.
A functioning experimentation practice, where the team ships, measures and learns on a short cycle.
An engineering organisation built out from its current base, with a strong bench of Engineering Managers and senior engineers.
Rewards established as a measurable contributor to retention and engagement across the customer base.
Clear architecture standards and engineering processes in place across the product units.
